before.label: Dephosphorylate RNA and ligate the 3′ IR800–biotin adapter
before.description: End-treated RNA fragments acquire the labeled DNA adapter at their 3′ ends while the complexes remain immunoprecipitated. The standalone adapter drawing is a reagent input, not a separate preparation reaction.
before.mechanism: T4 PNK dephosphorylates RNase-A- or RNase-1-digested complexes; T4 RNA Ligase 1 then joins the preadenylated DNA adapter to RNA 3′ ends. Internal IR800 supports nonisotopic detection, terminal biotin supports later affinity capture, and the adapter includes the depicted RT-priming region.
before.information_effect: The infrared label is attached through successful 3′ adapter ligation, so detection tracks adapter-bearing RNA complexes rather than merely a labeled free RNA 5′ end.

after.label: Dephosphorylate RNA ends and ligate the 3′ adapter
after.description: Dephosphorylate RNase-digested complexes with T4 PNK, then attach the preadenylated IR800–biotin DNA adapter to RNA 3′ ends using T4 RNA Ligase 1.
after.mechanism: Dephosphorylation prepares the RNase-digested RNA ends for ligation. The preadenylated adapter is the ligation substrate; its infrared dye supports nonisotopic detection, its terminal biotin supplies the later streptavidin handle, and its sequence supplies the RT priming interface.
after.information_effect: Covalently tagging RNA 3′ ends links infrared detection and later affinity recovery to adapter-ligated RNA rather than to all crosslinked molecules.

before.label: Reverse-transcribe, capture with streptavidin and elute cDNA
before.description: TGIRT-III copies adapter-primed RNA to cDNA. The cDNA–RNA hybrids are captured using the biotin-bearing RNA adapter on streptavidin beads; the reported cDNA-elution/RNA-degradation step then provides cDNA for circularization. These actions remain one composite block, correcting the catalogue caption “Immunopurify”.
before.mechanism: TGIRT-III reverse transcription at 60°C precedes streptavidin capture of cDNA–RNA hybrids. Capture is mediated by adapter biotin. The subsequent elution/RNA-degradation buffer contains P3short and MnCl2 and uses heating. The paper names this release step but does not specify a detailed molecular displacement pathway.
before.information_effect: RNA sequence is copied into DNA. For RT-terminated molecules, residual peptide–RNA crosslinks give an endpoint interpreted as one base 3′ of the contact. Biotin and IR800 reside on the RNA-linked adapter and are not asserted to be chemical modifications of the cDNA. The primer contributes the barcode region, 5′ phosphate and internal spacers.

after.label: Reverse-transcribe RNA, affinity-capture hybrids and release cDNA
after.description: Anneal the cDNA synthesis primer and copy recovered RNA with TGIRT-III at 60°C. Capture RNA–cDNA hybrids on streptavidin beads via the biotinylated RNA adapter, then degrade RNA and elute cDNA before circularization.
after.mechanism: The adapter supplies the RT primer-binding region. TGIRT-III makes RNA-derived cDNA at 60°C; the catalogue reports that this temperature melts secondary RNA structures to reduce reverse-transcription bias. RT can stop at the crosslinked peptide. Streptavidin binds the RNA adapter’s biotin to capture hybrids. The MnCl2-containing RNA-degradation/cDNA-elution step uses P3short oligonucleotide and releases cDNA. The cDNA primer supplies a 5′ phosphate, barcode and internal spacers; the adapter’s dye and biotin are on the RNA-side capture substrate, not modifications copied into DNA.
after.information_effect: RNA sequence and, for peptide-stopped molecules, the termination endpoint become DNA-encoded surrogates for RNA identity and the contact position. Primer-encoded barcode/index information is introduced. Subsequent sequencing and mapping are required to interpret these features as binding sites.

initial_review_requests.rationale: The candidate records TGIRT-III and 60°C in o6.description, but o6.mechanism never explains the catalogue-reported reason for this condition: melting secondary RNA structures to reduce bias. That explanation occurs only in o6.evidence. Add it to o6.mechanism as a reported catalogue claim, retaining the distinction that the primary methods confirm the enzyme and temperature rather than independently establishing the bias-reduction claim. This is a missing explanation of a retained, method-distinguishing operation; no added State or Operation, RT execution settings, or new research is needed.

evidence.locator: Pros: reported reason for thermostable RT at 60°C
evidence.quote: Uses thermostable reverse transcriptase at 60°C, reducing biases by melting secondary RNA structures1

0.2 μL of TIGRT-III reverse transcriptase (Ingex, #TGIRT50) was added to the annealed RNA and incubated at room temperature for 30 min. 1 μL of 25 mM dNTPs was added to the reaction, mixed well, and incubated in a thermocycler for 2 h at 60 °C.
cDNA-RNA hybrids were captured by addition of 5 μL of MyOne Streptavidin C1 Dynabeads (Thermo Fisher Scientific, #65001)

Beads were resuspended in 10 μL of cDNA elution/RNA degradation buffer (8.25 μL water, 1 μL of 1 μM P3short oligonucleotide, and 0.75 μL of 50 mM MnCl2) and placed in a thermocycler with the program: 5 min 95 °C, 1 min 75 °C, ramp 0.1° s−1 to 60 °C forever.

before.label: Mock-treat RNA without CMC
before.description: Process the parallel RNA preparation in BEU buffer without CMC, providing a background-stop control.
before.mechanism: The reported mock exposure uses BEU buffer without CMC.
before.information_effect: Preserves the comparator for CMC-independent RNA-sequence/structure-associated or other background RT stops.

after.label: Mock-treat RNA without CMC
after.description: Process the matched control fragments in the reported mock-treatment buffer without adding CMC.
after.mechanism: Omitting CMC prevents introduction of the treatment-dependent RT-blocking mark; RT stops in this branch provide a background comparison.
after.information_effect: The separately identified −CMC preparation supplies pseudouridine-independent RT-stop background, not a Ψ-specific endpoint signal.

before.label: Reverse-transcribe +CMC RNA
before.description: Synthesize cDNA from adaptor-ligated RNA; CMC-modified Ψ can terminate extension, producing truncated cDNAs together with other RT products.
before.mechanism: AMV reverse transcriptase extends the adaptor-complementary, 5′-phosphorylated RT primer. The source reports arrest one nucleotide 3′ of CMC-modified Ψ.
before.information_effect: RNA sequence becomes DNA sequence; termination position is retained as a cDNA endpoint. The RNA Ψ/CMC group itself is not copied as that chemical modification into DNA.

after.label: Reverse-transcribe adapter-ligated RNA
after.description: Independently anneal the 5′-phosphorylated adapter-complementary RT primer and extend it with AMV-RT on each RNA-fragment preparation, producing RNA-derived cDNA products, including truncated cDNAs.
after.mechanism: The adapter-complementary primer initiates RNA copying. In +CMC RNA, the retained Ψ-dependent mark can stop RT one nucleotide 3′ of Ψ; background termination also occurs and is measured by the parallel −CMC preparation.
after.information_effect: cDNA sequence and its termination boundary encode RNA origin and RT-stop position. The RNA chemical modification is not copied into DNA. Only +CMC-versus−CMC comparison after mapping can attribute excess stops to candidate Ψ sites.

other_method_checks.previous_strength: Distinguishes combined 5fC/5caC signal from individual-base identification; explains collapse of original C and 5mC after protective methylation.
Reporter is ligated synthetic DNA probes, not RNA-derived cDNA; barcode identifies sample, not an individual original RNA molecule.

findings: irCLIP names dephosphorylation and ligation in description; those details already existed in the archived mechanism. This is improved placement, not new scientific discovery.
irCLIP reviewer requested the temperature-related rationale already present in evidence. Author amended mechanism; fresh review remains pending.
Pseudo-seq separates +CMC and mock information meaning and states the mapping/control inference dependency. It passed review without revision.
Pseudo-seq has shared Operations with separate condition States and explicit per-condition effects; fewer Operations does not establish higher accuracy.
This preserves the local-condition principle tested on November 8; do not claim it is newly discovered or proven better than all prior refined runs.
Source-attribution wording remains in some fields. Distinguish unnecessary reading/grouping commentary from consequential qualification of a reported but unverified benefit.
One output per method cannot establish a prompt effect or reduced hallucination rate.
